title: The Pressure Test
thread: Soaring oil and rigid interest rates squeezed tech stocks and crypto, even as European equities and global dealmakers pushed ahead.
summary: Brent crude climbed toward $110 a barrel and the US 10-year yield reached 5.24%, triggering a steep 4.48% drop in the tech-heavy Nasdaq. While crypto saw $409 million in ETF outflows and founders cashed out billions, European stocks rallied and Southeast Asia celebrated a record-breaking tech IPO.

sections.p: Brent crude climbed 4.91% to close at $109.86 as Middle East geopolitical tensions and Washington's waiver on Russian sanctions stirred energy markets.
The US 10-year Treasury yield surged to a high of 5.24% before settling at 5.10%, maintaining intense pressure on global borrowing costs.
Tech valuations tumbled with the Nasdaq shedding 4.48%, while CoreWeave insiders revealed $3.3 billion in post-IPO stock sales.
A stark regional divide emerged as European indexes gained over 2% while Tokyo's Nikkei sank 5.37% and Singapore's exports soared 68.4%.
Bitcoin dipped below $81,000 amid $409.2 million in spot ETF outflows, while the UK FCA opened licensing gateways and Turkish police arrested Hex's founder.
Gold traded steadily near record highs at $4,181.10 an ounce as investors sought refuge against persistent inflation.
